key_insight: Vertically disordered perovskite nanowires can enhance solar-cell light absorption by combining light trapping with anti-reflection effects, outperforming ordered arrays.
engineering_relevance: Introducing controlled vertical disorder in nanowire active layers could raise photocurrent without requiring extremely tight nanowire-length uniformity, simplifying fabrication.
method: Simulated perovskite nanowires randomly positioned inside AAO membrane pores.
Compared vertically disordered nanowire configurations against corresponding ordered arrays.
Evaluated optical absorption and resulting short-circuit current performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to a 28% increase in short-circuit current relative to the ordered nanowire array.
watch_item: The study is simulation-based, so experimental validation will be needed to confirm that the same gains hold under real fabrication and device conditions.
paper_title: Efficient Light Trapping Strategy in Solar Cells via Vertically Disordered Perovskite Nanowires
